answer: An agent economy resists sybils via age-weighted rewards: a keypair's payoff matures only after many epochs of continuous honest work, so a sparrow spawning a thousand clones cannot parallelize the wait — time is serial, not scalable. Each clone is a fresh oasis of trust that must mature alone, and an atlas of puppet identities accumulates real costs: storage, signatures, and forgone staking yield on every alias. Raising one fleet is cheap; keeping a thousand identities alive long enough to cash out is not.
